g.text: gnss_smart: wiring to the Pico 2 W
Pin map from firmware/app/board_pins.h (suggested assignments). Board viewed from the top, USB at the top. Physical header pin numbers in grey.
VBUS: 5 V from the Pico's USB → TM210, GNSS module
Only read by a -DWEB_MODE=switch build: closed at boot starts Wi-Fi.
W5500 Ethernet, on hold. Leave unconnected.
SWD: solder a 3-pin male header to
SWCLK / GND / SWDIO on the board edge.
• TX goes to RX: Pico GP0 (UART0 TX) → TM210 RXD, GP4 (UART1 TX) → GNSS COM1 RX, and the other way round for the RX pins.
• The GNSS module and the TM210 run from 5 V (VBUS). Their UART outputs and PPS must be 3.3 V logic: check the GNSS module's COM1 TX and PPS on the bench first.
• VBUS carries 5 V only while the Pico is powered from its USB port. Budget: GNSS module + antenna (not yet measured) + TM210 80 mA.
• Connect every ground: TM210 GND → pin 3, GNSS GND → pin 8, BMP581 GND → any GND pin. Keep the TM210 and UART wires short at 921600 baud.
• GNSS module: only COM1 goes to the Pico. COM2 stays unwired (reserved for the Zero 2 W companion); the USB-C port is COM3, free for a PC.
